title: Monopoly 10x Thinking
equation: Monopoly Position = (Performance Multiple + Switching Cost + Defensibility) ÷ 3
hook: Being a little better than the competition just starts a price war. You need to be way better at one thing.
statement: Aim to be 10 times better on the one thing customers care about most, enough to own the market.
explainer: Ten percent better gets matched in a quarter. Ten times better changes what customers expect. Then switching costs and a real moat keep competitors from catching up.
sop: Find the one thing customers care about most.
Set a target to be 10 times better on it.
Build lasting advantages like network effects, scale, or brand.
Protect that moat as you grow.
Reinvest profit into widening the gap.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Performance Multiple 8, Switching Cost 5, Defensibility 6. (8 + 5 + 6) ÷ 3 = 6.3. Higher means competitors can't catch up any time soon. Lower means your edge is small and easy to match.
question: Name the one thing you could realistically be 10 times better at than anyone else.
closing_statement: Ten percent better gets copied. Ten times doesn't.
caption:
Principle Nº 294: Monopoly 10x Thinking

Being a little better than the competition just starts a price war. You need to be way better at one thing.

Aim to be 10 times better on the one thing customers care about most, enough to own the market.

Your turn: Name the one thing you could realistically be 10 times better at than anyone else.
